qs.q: Overflow can be detected by XOR-ing the two bits of carry-in and carry-out.
e: Overflow occurs only when two positive numbers give a negative result, or two negative numbers give a positive result.
In hardware this is detected by comparing the carry into the sign (MSB) column (c-in) with the carry out of it (c-out).
If they are different, overflow occurs; if they are the same, there is no overflow. 'Different' is exactly what XOR computes, so the statement is True.

qs.q: The flag V is set to one when ____.
e: The condition code register has four bits: N, Z, V and C.
N is set if the result is negative (MSB = 1). Z is set if the result is zero (all bits 0).
V is set if the operation produced an overflow. C is set if the operation produced a carry (borrow on subtraction).
So V is set when the result causes overflow.

qs.q: Each shift to the right ____ the number by ____.
e: Shifting right moves every bit one position to a lower weight (power of 2), so the value is divided by 2.
Example: 1000 (8) shifted right becomes 0100 (4), then 0010 (2).
So each right shift reduces the number by half (a left shift doubles it).

qs.q: To multiply 8 times 5, this can be done as ____.
e: Each left shift multiplies a number by 2, so shifting left by n positions multiplies it by $2^n$.
8 = $2^3$, so 5 x 8 = 5 x $2^3$ = shift 5 left by 3 positions.
Check: 5 = 101; shifting left 3 positions gives 101000 = 40 = 5 x 8.
Right shifts divide the number, so they cannot be used for multiplication.

qs.q: An unsigned number operation uses the ____ to verify the result.
e: For unsigned numbers there is no sign bit, so every bit is magnitude.
If the addition produces a carry out of the MSB (the C flag is set), the result does not fit in the available bits, so it is wrong.
The overflow flag V is meant for signed (2's complement) numbers, which is why the unsigned check uses the carry-out.

qs.q: In a normal n-bit adder, to find out whether an overflow has occurred we make use of a(n) ____ gate.
e: Overflow occurs when the carry into the MSB column (c-in) and the carry out of the MSB column (c-out) are different.
A gate whose output is 1 only when its two inputs differ is the XOR gate.
So V = c-in XOR c-out.

qs.q: Carry flag: this flag is set to 1 when there is a signed overflow.
e: The C (carry) bit is set when the operation produces a carry out of the MSB (a borrow on subtraction), which indicates an unsigned out-of-range result.
Signed overflow is indicated by a different flag, V.
So the statement is False. Note: the source exam key marks True, which contradicts the lecture.

qs.q: Sign flag: this flag is set to 1 when the result is negative.
e: The sign flag corresponds to the N bit of the condition code register.
N is set if the result of the operation is negative, i.e. its MSB = 1.
So the statement is True.
